inspection_summary: Inspected all 436 lines. The source reframes finite RH verification as rigorous separation of zeros through sign changes of a real-valued function, develops a cost-aware search for the two sign changes missing inside a Gram block, records a conservative two-method error-certification layer, and audits how argument shifts and block length affect the resulting statistics. Exact formulas and several dense tables have OCR damage; only conclusions recoverable from the checked prose are accepted, while exact damaged cells are quarantined.

accepted_units.title: Completed-function symmetry reframes the Riemann hypothesis
accepted_units.why_material: The prose converts the hypothesis into a real-zero statement for an even entire function and equivalently into a critical-line statement for nonreal zeta zeros, then uses conjugation symmetry to restrict attention to positive height.
accepted_units.context_note: The defining displays are OCR-damaged, so the unit preserves only the equivalences and symmetry restriction explicitly stated in the prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the completed-function and real-variable representations; exact normalization symbols in lines 20-30 require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel evaluation replaces the earlier Euler-Maclaurin computational regime
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes hand or desk-calculator work based on Euler-Maclaurin summation from later electronic computation based on the Riemann-Siegel formula, tying representation choice to a large change in reachable zero counts.
accepted_units.context_note: The listed investigators and counts serve as source-internal evidence for the stated methodological transition, not as a general performance law.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the named summation formulas and computing regimes; no damaged formula is needed for the comparison.

accepted_units.title: Finite zero verification becomes costed sign-change separation
accepted_units.why_material: The paper states that verification over a finite range is performed by separating zeros of the real function Z(t), equivalently by finding enough sign changes, and identifies Z-evaluation as the dominant cost. It then compares evaluation counts and gives a source-specific lower bound for methods evaluating every Gram point.
accepted_units.context_note: The final certification relies on a theorem cited later; this span supplies the computational reduction and cost model rather than a stand-alone proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the Z(t) and Gram-point representations; numerical ranges and timings are evidence for these implementations only.

accepted_units.title: Reduce a Gram block to locating two missing sign changes
accepted_units.why_material: Once a block of length L has implicitly supplied L-2 sign changes, the search is reduced to two remaining changes that must share a Gram interval. The program ranks the two outer intervals by endpoint-value evidence, applies parabolic interpolation, then searches the other outer interval and finally the interior or full length-two block.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 99-103 are necessary setup omitted from the prior v1 span; the strategy is an empirically ordered search, not a theorem that the changes are normally outermost.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Gram-block boundaries and endpoint evaluations of Z(t); the garbled subscripts are recoverable from the checked prose but exact notation should be verified against the scan if reused symbolically.

accepted_units.title: Escalate unresolved blocks to preserved plots and manual inspection
accepted_units.why_material: The automated routine records unresolved blocks instead of silently treating its heuristic as conclusive: it emits a message and plot, continues provisionally, and subjects the exceptional cases to later inspection, including adjacent blocks. Extending beyond the target range and invoking the cited theorem then closes the finite-zero claim.
accepted_units.context_note: The source says the program proceeds by pretending the missing changes were found, so the later inspection and cited theorem are essential safeguards; this span does not reproduce that theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on human-readable plots and Theorem 3.2 of the cited earlier paper, whose content is not imported here.

accepted_units.title: Conservative two-method error control certifies signs of Z(t)
accepted_units.why_material: The computation combines a Riemann-Siegel approximation, analytic remainder control, interpolation and machine-error accounting, then uses fixed bounds more conservative than the derived upper bounds. A higher-precision method is available when the fast method is inconclusive, and the source reports that it always determined the sign rigorously in the run described.
accepted_units.context_note: The semantic certification pipeline is recoverable, but the displayed bound at lines 173-178 is corrupt and its coefficients or exponents must not be learned from this text layer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong formula and hardware dependency: the exact error display requires scan verification, while the accepted claim is limited to the prose-stated bound hierarchy and sign decision.

accepted_units.title: Small argument shifts reduce expensive fallbacks but break strict count accumulation
accepted_units.why_material: When method A cannot rigorously determine a sign, the program tries small shifts before invoking method B. This optimization means some evaluations occur near rather than exactly at Gram points, so its statistics are not strictly accumulable with Brent's even though the paper presents them together.
accepted_units.context_note: The span explicitly separates computational convenience from exact statistical comparability.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the Gram-point sampling convention and the method-A/method-B decision hierarchy.

accepted_units.title: Shifted sampling can change the observed class of a Rosser-rule exception
accepted_units.why_material: The source warns that shifted Gram-point evaluation may miss or reclassify exceptions, gives a concrete zero-pattern mechanism for such reclassification, and distinguishes six exception types while noting that one type had not been observed.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact visual definitions of all six types are delegated to an OCR-damaged table; only the detection-bias mechanism and prose-stated occurrence claims are accepted here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Gram-block zero patterns and Table 2; exact table geometry and symbols require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Selected subranges can efficiently screen for Rosser-rule exceptions
accepted_units.why_material: A different method searches only selected small ranges inside a height interval and nevertheless recovers all exceptions in one comparison range and most in another, showing that rare-event detection need not exhaustively scan the whole interval in the same way.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction of the selected ranges is not present, so the unit records comparative evidence rather than a reproducible algorithm.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the cited method's range-selection rule, which is outside the inspected source.

accepted_units.title: Independent programs closely agree on Gram-block counts despite shifted sampling
accepted_units.why_material: On an overlapping range the two programs give extremely close counts for short blocks and identical counts for longer blocks. The surrounding summaries record a stable empirical distribution of block lengths and of zeros per Gram interval, while explicitly retaining the possibility that shifts obscured some first occurrences.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose supports the agreement and percentage summaries; exact cells in Tables 3-5 are OCR-risky and are not asserted beyond those prose summaries.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Gram-block classifications and tabular counts; exact row values and some type labels require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The outer-interval heuristic is conditional on Gram-block length
accepted_units.why_material: The counted block types support the outer-first search for lengths two through five, but for lengths at least six the missing zeros increasingly move one interval inward; only one length-seven block places them in an outer interval. Thus an efficiency heuristic validated in common short blocks does not extrapolate uniformly to rarer long blocks.
accepted_units.context_note: The qualitative conclusion is explicit in the prose; exact Table 6 cells and percentages are quarantined because of tabular OCR damage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the block-type and missing-zero-location representation; scan verification is required for exact counts in Table 6.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Cost-aware certified zero separation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source organizes finite verification as a layered pipeline: use structural information to minimize Z-evaluations, search likely intervals first, escalate unresolved blocks, and reserve conservative or higher-precision sign certification for ambiguous cases.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The final implication to the zero claim depends on a cited theorem not reproduced here, and the exact error formula is OCR-defective.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A search heuristic has an empirically bounded regime
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Outer-interval priority is efficient because common short blocks support it, but block-type statistics reveal a qualitative location shift for longer blocks, motivating a length-conditioned search policy.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is solver- and range-specific empirical evidence, not a proof of a universal block-length law; exact table cells require scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Optimization of observations can alter the measured exception process
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Argument shifts and selective-range screening reduce computational effort but can change detection or classification of rare exceptions, so cross-program overlap checks and explicit sampling provenance are part of the evidential method rather than incidental bookkeeping.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The overlap comparisons are bounded to stated ranges, and the source does not provide the construction of the alternative selected ranges.
